name: Ammihud
overview: Ammihud was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim known primarily as the father of Elishama. His identity is established in the context of the Israelite tribal structure, with no additional personal notes recorded. He is recognized within Scripture for his familial role and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Ammihud means '[my] people have majesty,' reflecting a sense of dignity or honor associated with his lineage. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance that connects to his tribal identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ammihud as the father of Elishama and the father of Ladan, indicating his role as a patriarch within his family. Additionally, he is explicitly noted as a descendant of Ephraim, linking him to one of the prominent tribes of Israel.
scriptureSignificance: Ammihud's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his position within the tribe of Ephraim and his role as the father of Elishama, who is mentioned in the census of Israel. This connection situates Ammihud within the lineage of God's chosen people, highlighting the continuity of God's covenant through tribal and familial lines.
